newsitem.title: UK: United union to vote on industrial action.
newsitem.headline: United union to vote on industrial action.

text.p: UK electricity company United Utilities Plc is facing the threat of industrial action from union members, the union representing United's workers said

The Amalgamated Engineering and Electrical Union (AEEU) said on Friday it would start balloting around 1,200 members on Monday on industrial action over what it calls the company's intention to remove union rights from a section of its workforce.
A spokesman for United told Reuters: "We are disappointed that action is being threatened before consultation has taken place."
United announced plans on Thursday to transfer its Norweb metering services into its Vertex division.

The union said 90 staff were affected by United's offer of a 12-percent wage rise to its metering service staff in return for signing a personal contract which would take them outside collective bargaining arrangements.

If they refused to do this their union rights would be removed anyway as they were being transferred to United Utilities billing and servicing arm, Vertex, where there was no collective bargaining agreement, the AEEU said.
"We consider it important that we harmonise conditions of employment as far as possible for the staff concerned," the United spokesman said.
The ballot will ask members if they are prepared to either take strike action or action short of a strike, which might include bans on working overtime and a work to rule.
